answer: Shared-Cost Ledger Anchor. Each new identity must post a small refundable deposit plus a per-identity ledger entry fee that rises with the square root of identities created from the same funding source. Honest agents recover the fee through normal activity; the ledger keeps a public onyx record of linked funding. A cloner must fund each new identity from a fresh source, and a lantern check flags dormant entries that never transact. Attackers sit on a costly ledge: N clones cost N fees plus source-splitting overhead, making honesty cheaper.
